As far as p2p I would like to set something up. I think the site has a responsibility to be there to serve content so a p2p reliant system probably isn't best but I'd like to see something with layers. Central server -> CDN -> p2p CDN.

My ideal is that if the p2p CDN is in that any bytes served near the play position are served by the CDN but subsequent bytes are loaded by p2p to reduce load on the CDN. If the p2p isn't able to keep up then the player position will end up near the load position at some point and the CDN will take over.

Central server -> CDN -> p2p CDN

This is basically what I mean. The video is on the site's server but p2p video is used to offload the server usage and bandwidth costs. Especially when a video is going viral.

Supposedly Bittorrent Inc. figured out something but nothing ever came of it.

https://torrentfreak.com/bittorrent-new-live-streaming-platform-130312/

BitComet had some tech that handled ways to download from multiple sources including http & ftp years ago. However, its been years since I've used their software.

So there is a turn key solution. It's called p2pCDN but the problem is that it's exactly the opposite. It does p2p then falls back to CDN. It takes some time for the p2p to timeout. For small videos that aren't navigated to via a link the odds of a peer are really low so the odds of a pause loading are high. The site would need a lot more traffic before p2p do anything and for sure doing it the opposite to p2pCDN is the way to go. This is in the works, but I just had a recent epiphany about how the cdn needs to work if it's also going to help expand storage so I'm realizing we're a long way out.

An alternative because it respects people's freedom of choice is that because this CDN has to be redundant to operate as a storage people could volunteer nodes with control over storage and bandwidth limits. I then could up the redundancy to three instead of two. People could set up nodes as small as they like.
